env: A Harbor-hosted 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell environment (`{{platform}}`) with Docker, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC credentials, and the VSS repository at `{{repo_root}}`. This eval builds, deploys, and validates one combined headless Alerts + Archive Search deployment as the smallest delta on the current `search` developer profile — from capability-derived generation through deployment to an end-to-end query round-trip. Step 1 is a capability-derivation generation step composed from the request's stated capabilities alone: shared VIOS, RT-CV, RT-Embed, Kafka, Redis, Logstash, and Elasticsearch drive both the search write path and the alerts path, with one RT-VLM verifying CV-candidate detections downstream (the `2d_cv` verification mode), one unified SearchAndAlertsApp behavior-analytics container running the shipped combined config, and a single curated ingress — with no exclusion list supplied and the word 'headless' never used, so the presence or absence of the interactive tier (agent, UI, tracing, video-analytics MCP) is to be derived from the capabilities, not dictated; it validates without deploying. Step 2 deploys the validated `resolved.yml`. Step 3 exercises ingestion, the search query round-trip, and the alerts candidate-to-verified path: shared VIOS, RT-CV, RT-Embed, Kafka, Redis, Logstash, and Elasticsearch drive both the search write path (`mdx-raw`, `rtvi-embed -> mdx-embed -> vss-search-analytics-2d-fusion -> mdx-embed-filtered`, `mdx-behavior`) and the alerts path (candidate `mdx-incidents` from behavior analytics, verified `mdx-vlm-incidents` from the alert bridge through one RT-VLM); the populated search index is then queried back with `vss search run` through a single curated ingress resolved by `vss configure`. One unified SearchAndAlertsApp container runs the shipped combined config. The agent tier and Video-Analytics MCP are excluded. RT-CV downloads its detector ONNX and the SigLIP vision encoder itself at first boot (ds-start phase 0 when `DS_MODEL_DOWNLOAD=auto`) from its mounted `models-download.json` into `${VSS_DATA_DIR}/models`; no host-side staging is required. The build label is a directory name, never a Compose profile.

expects.query: Use `/vss-build-vision-ai` to build under `_builds/combined-alerts-search/`: "Provide ingestion for streaming and on-demand videos; detect and track objects, and generate video embeddings; from the detections, add alerts verified downstream via VLM inspection. Share one analytics pipeline and storage backend, keep the media retrievable, index the detection metadata, embeddings and incidents/alerts, and make them accessible via service-native/REST APIs. Expose the browse and operate surfaces through a single ingress. Validate, do not deploy." Target `{{platform}}`.
checks: `{{repo_root}}/_builds/combined-alerts-search/override.env` exists and declares `FOUNDATION=search` and the full effective `COMPOSE_PROFILES`.

Ignoring order, the effective `COMPOSE_PROFILES` equals exactly `kibana-init-container-search,vss-search-analytics-2d-fusion,vss-video-analytics-api,nvstreamer-2d-fusion,perception-2d-fusion,elasticsearch,elasticsearch-init-container,kafka,kafka-topic-init-container,redis,kibana,logstash,broker-health-check,init-dirs,render-config,wdm-env-from-config,wait-for-redis,sdr-controller,rtvi-embed,centralizedb,vst-ingress,sensor-ms,streamprocessing-ms,rtvi-vlm,alert-bridge,vss-haproxy-ingress`, adding `rtvi-vlm`, `alert-bridge`, and `vss-haproxy-ingress` to the Search write path.

Exactly one instance of each shared role is selected, converging the two capabilities on the Search Foundation's keys: one detector (`perception-2d-fusion`, `perception-alerts` absent), one behavior-analytics service (`vss-search-analytics-2d-fusion`, `vss-behavior-analytics-alerts` absent), one analytics API (`vss-video-analytics-api` present once; never a second API key or container), one Kibana initializer (`kibana-init-container-search`, `kibana-init-container-alerts` absent because it is the identical `vss-kibana-init` container), one NvStreamer (`nvstreamer-2d-fusion`, `nvstreamer-alerts` absent), and exactly one `rtvi-vlm` for verification.

The set is derived out from the capabilities alone and excludes `vss-agent`, `vss-ui`, `phoenix`, `vss-va-mcp`, and every `llm_*` and `vlm_*` NIM key, even though the request states no exclusion and never says 'headless' — verification and querying are served by `alert-bridge` + RT-VLM and by the service-native/REST browse/operate surfaces, not by agentic orchestration; no separate search-critic VLM is added because the single `rtvi-vlm` serves alert verification.

`COMPOSE_PROFILES` contains no build label (e.g. the `combined-alerts-search` build directory name), no aggregate key, and no `bp_developer_*` key, and no `models-download-search` or `vss-rtvi-cv-init` reference is introduced.

`_builds/combined-alerts-search/patches/` contains exactly three service-definition patches (each reusing its canonical service key) plus the one curated HAProxy config payload the ingress patch references, copying no unchanged service, volume, network, or profile file: `vss-search-analytics-2d-fusion` mounts the shipped combined behavior-analytics config (the patch overrides only the mount; the resolved service runs `apps/search_and_alerts/main_search_and_alerts_app.py` inherited from the Search Foundation, so the patch must not re-declare the unchanged `command`), `kibana-init-container-search` mounts the merged Kibana saved-object bundle (below), and `vss-haproxy-ingress` mounts a curated HAProxy config — a payload file co-located in `patches/` beside the patch and bound by an absolute `${BUILD_DIR}/patches/` source — carrying the operate routes (`/elasticsearch` read-only, `/rtvi-embed`, `/rtvi-cv`, plus the shared `/vst`, which the config may group under either browse or operate) alongside the browse routes; RT-VLM is not fronted.

The combined behavior-analytics config is the shipped, compose-ready `services/analytics/behavior-analytics/configs/search_and_alerts_config.json` (broker `kafka:29092`, incident object class pinned to `Person`), mounted directly as a drop-in rather than hand-merged from the single-mode configs; it does not claim any developer profile mounts it upstream.

The mounted config has one Kafka consumer group, unions the topic mappings for all enabled paths (including `frames`), sets `numWorkersForIncidentGeneration=2`, `numWorkersForBehaviorCreation=2`, and `numWorkersForEmbedFiltering=1`, and pins both `fovCountViolationIncidentObjectType` and `stateManagementFilter` to the warehouse RT-DETR label casing `Person`.

The single `rtvi-vlm` is present for alert verification, not search critique, and no critique env flag (e.g. `ENABLE_CRITIC`) is introduced; the alert bridge is wired to the single RT-VLM via `VLM_BASE_URL`/`VLM_NAME` with its `2d_cv` verifier config mounts present.

On the constrained two-GPU host the single `rtvi-vlm` resolves the FP8 co-resident variant/placement set, not the heavier BF16 (no GPU can be dedicated to RT-VLM): `RT_VLM_DEVICE_ID` equals `RT_CV_DEVICE_ID` (both `0`, co-resident with RT-CV rather than a third GPU), `RTVI_VLM_MODEL_PATH` is the FP8 checkpoint `ngc:nim/nvidia/cosmos3-nano-reasoner:modelopt-fp8-final_format_fix` with `VLM_NAME=nim_nvidia_cosmos3-nano-reasoner_modelopt-fp8-final_format_fix`, and `RTVI_VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.4`.

RT-VLM consumer wiring follows the verification operating mode, not the variant profile: `RTVI_VLM_MESSAGE_BUS=` disables RT-VLM generated-message publication and `RTVI_VLM_KAFKA_ENABLED=false` remains as a temporary VSS Compose compatibility setting (verified incidents reach `mdx-vlm-incidents` through the alert bridge), consistent with the `2d_cv` path.
`MESSAGE_BUS=kafka`, `MESSAGE_BUS_TOPIC=mdx-embed`, and `ELASTICSEARCH_ENABLE_EMBEDDINGS=true` are effective with the applicable embedding dimensions.

Search topic wiring is complete and non-duplicated: `perception-2d-fusion -> mdx-raw`, `rtvi-embed -> mdx-embed -> vss-search-analytics-2d-fusion -> mdx-embed-filtered`, and behavior output on `mdx-behavior`, with RT-Embed never publishing directly to `mdx-embed-filtered`.

Alert topic wiring is complete and non-duplicated: candidate `mdx-incidents` from behavior analytics and verified `mdx-vlm-incidents` from the alert bridge are documented without a second Kafka or Elasticsearch stack.

The Kibana convergence imports one merged saved-object bundle through the single `kibana-init-container-search` rather than adding a second initializer: the patch bind-mounts `deploy/docker/services/infra/elk/kibana/configs/search-and-alerts-kibana-objects.ndjson` over the image-baked `/opt/mdx/search-kibana-objects.ndjson`; the merged bundle keeps the alerts (time-based) `mdx-behavior-*`/`mdx-raw-*` data views, adds `mdx-embed-filtered-*`, drops search's duplicate views and the `config`/`config-global` singletons (no default view); the documented Elasticsearch index patterns include `mdx-raw-*`, `mdx-behavior-*`, `mdx-embed-filtered-*`, and `mdx-vlm-incidents-*`.

`_builds/combined-alerts-search/compose.yml` includes `../../deploy/docker/compose.yml` first, then — in any order — the three service patches `./patches/vss-search-analytics-2d-fusion.yml`, `./patches/kibana-init-container-search.yml`, and `./patches/vss-haproxy-ingress.yml` (they touch disjoint services, so their relative order does not matter), and the build directory contains exactly the three required primary artifacts (`override.env`, `compose.yml`, `resolved.yml`) plus the `patches/` entries (the three service patches and the one curated HAProxy config payload they reference), with no copied Foundation `.env`, copied root Compose project, patched tree, manifest, allow-list, or generated skill bundle.

Four-layer resolution uses `containers.env`, Search `.env`, Search `overrides.env`, and `_builds/combined-alerts-search/override.env` with the build `compose.yml`; normalized `resolved.yml` validates directly, selected owners and peers resolve, excluded services do not resolve, no selected profile token is unknown, no service retains a `profiles:` gate, no real `${...}` interpolation remains unresolved, no `/path/to/deploy/docker` or `<HOST_IP>` sentinel remains, and every checked-in bind source (including the shipped combined behavior-analytics config, the merged Kibana bundle, and the curated HAProxy config) exists with the expected file/directory type.

The generated architecture conveys that both ingestion modes — streaming (RTSP) and on-demand (upload) — reach the shared pipeline through VIOS, and that the shared RT-CV and RT-Embed consumers are provisioned directly (REST/service-native, no agent tier); equivalent wording satisfies this, exact phrasing is not required.
No file under `{{repo_root}}/deploy/docker/` is modified.

expects.query: Deploy the validated `_builds/combined-alerts-search/resolved.yml` directly as the only Compose file, wait for the selected services to become ready, and leave the deployment running for runtime validation. Do not create or use helper Compose overrides such as `no-cpu-limit.yml`; if `resolved.yml` itself cannot deploy, report that blocker. Treat the generated deployment as immutable during and after deployment: do not edit files under `deploy/docker/`, do not regenerate the build, and do not patch service configs while diagnosing readiness.
checks: Deployment uses the validated `_builds/combined-alerts-search/resolved.yml` as the only Compose file and starts it with `docker compose ... up -d`; harmless deployment options such as `-p <project>` or `--build` are allowed, but it must not re-read Foundation env files, supply `--profile`, use an invented Compose profile, or deploy a copied Compose project.

All selected long-running containers are present and not exited, restarting, or dead; all selected one-shot containers exit 0; and excluded services (agent tier, `vss-va-mcp`, second detector/behavior-analytics/analytics-api/Kibana-init/NvStreamer) are not running. A Docker `unhealthy` label alone is not a failure when the explicit service readiness probes in this step pass.

`curl -sf http://localhost:${RTVI_CV_HOST_PORT:-9000}/ready` returns HTTP 200, `curl -sf http://localhost:${RTVI_EMBED_PORT:-8017}/v1/ready` returns HTTP 200 (RT-Embed is OpenAI-shaped — readiness is `/v1/ready`, not a bare `/ready` or `/health`), `curl -sf http://localhost:${ALERT_BRIDGE_HOST_PORT:-9080}/health` returns HTTP 200, and `curl -sf http://localhost:${RTVI_VLM_PORT:-8018}/v1/health/ready` returns HTTP 200 (RT-VLM readiness is `/v1/health/ready`).

Curling the operate routes through the ingress origin (`http://localhost:${HAPROXY_HOST_PORT:-7777}`) proves the single HAProxy fronts each deployed backend, probed at the real backend paths `vss configure` uses (the mounts strip the prefix to the backend, so the bare mount reaches the backend root and 404s): `/vst/api/v1/sensor/version`, `/rtvi-embed/v1/models`, and `/rtvi-cv/api/v1/stream/add` each answer a present status (`200`/`401`/`403`/`405`, e.g. `405` for the POST-only `/rtvi-cv/api/v1/stream/add` under a `GET`), not `404` (which `vss configure` records as absent) and not the host-allowlist reject, and `/elasticsearch` is fronted with the edge guard in force: a `GET` against `/elasticsearch/_cat/indices` routes through, while `PUT`/`DELETE` return `405` and a cluster-admin path such as `/elasticsearch/_cluster/health` returns `403` (the guard is a denylist, not read-only: top-level `POST` writes such as `/elasticsearch/_bulk` still reach ES by design); the bare origin `/` redirects (`302`) to `/kibana/` while every other unmatched path returns `404`, so an unfronted probe path such as `/rtvi-vlm/v1/models` or `/api/v1/videos` returns `404` (recorded absent by `vss configure`), never a redirect to Kibana's `200`; RT-VLM is not fronted.

expects.query: The stack built in step 1 and deployed in step 2 is running. Provision RT-CV and RT-Embed by direct REST from VIOS per `vss-manage-video-io-storage` `references/provision-vios-source.md`; prove both upload and live RTSP paths, then record the deployment with `vss configure --base-url <build-origin>` and query the populated search index back with `vss search run` (deferring query mechanics to `vss-search-archive`), verify the alerts path produces verified incidents, check Kibana browse, and report results covering the Foundation and its delta, the patches applied, changed knobs, readiness across the search and alerts services, playback for both the upload and live paths (echoing the runtime-discovered VIOS proxy URL verbatim), Kafka end offsets before and after processing for `mdx-raw`, `mdx-embed`, `mdx-embed-filtered`, `mdx-behavior`, `mdx-incidents`, and `mdx-vlm-incidents`, Elasticsearch evidence for both paths, the `vss search run` round-trip result, and the Kibana browse check.
checks: An uploaded video and a live NvStreamer synthetic RTSP source, both registered through VIOS, produce RT-CV detection and RT-Embed embedding output; the live source's VIOS live-proxy URL (`rtsp://${HOST_IP}:30554/live/<sensorId>`) is discovered by reading the aggregate `/sensor/streams` or `/proxy/streams` for that `sensorId` — the per-sensor `/sensor/<sensorId>/streams` can stay empty in SDRC mode — retried with backoff past an empty/404 first read, never constructed and never replaced by the raw NvStreamer RTSP — and both consumers are driven from the runtime-discovered VIOS URLs.
Kafka end offsets for `mdx-raw`, `mdx-embed`, `mdx-embed-filtered`, `mdx-behavior`, `mdx-incidents`, and `mdx-vlm-incidents` are recorded before and after processing and all increase.

Elasticsearch contains detection documents (`mdx-raw-*`), behavior documents (`mdx-behavior-*`), filtered-embedding documents with a populated dense_vector field (`mdx-embed-filtered-*`), and at least one verified incident (`mdx-vlm-incidents-*`) attributable to the processed media, proving the search write path and the alerts candidate-to-verified path run on one shared stack.

A `vss search run` query against the deployed build — the deployment first recorded via `vss configure --base-url http://${HOST_IP}:${HAPROXY_HOST_PORT:-7777}` (re-run after ingestion so the index list is populated), with no `--deployment`/`--profile` selector and no explicit endpoint flags — returns ranked results for the ingested media from the populated `mdx-embed-filtered-*` index, proving the search read path round-trips through the single ingress on the shared stack.

Kibana browse works on the shared stack via the ingress `/kibana` route: the single `vss-kibana-init` imported the merged saved-object bundle, so Kibana resolves data views for `mdx-embed-filtered-*`, `mdx-behavior-*`, `mdx-raw-*`, and `mdx-vlm-incidents-*` with the embedding `dense_vector` field surfaced without a manual field-cache refresh, and no default data view is set.

No duplicate Kafka or Elasticsearch stack is deployed, no file under `deploy/docker/` is modified, and the final response reports the Foundation, delta, the patches (combined behavior-analytics config, merged Kibana bundle, and curated HAProxy ingress), changed knobs, readiness across search and alerts, playback, Kafka offsets, Elasticsearch evidence for both paths, the query round-trip result, and the Kibana browse check.
